skip_reason: Not a sales call — post-move service recovery. Sergio (Houston branch manager) called an already-completed customer to collect feedback on a two-day move that ran over estimate, then resolved a billing dispute by offering a $520 refund to match the $3,940 the customer had agreed to in person. No quote request, no pricing pitch, no move being scoped or booked; the only forward-looking exchange was a one-line answer that the branch books 2–3 weeks out when she asked about a future move. Existing-move logistics / customer-service call per the skip rule. Transcript is also heavily garbled with a dropped-call segment and the customer speaking to people in her office mid-call.
top_strength: Not scored (skip). Worth noting for the branch anyway: Sergio pulled the contract live, quantified the overage himself ($5,320 billed, $1,000 already discounted for the added mover, $520 over the agreed $3,940), proactively offered the $520 back without being asked, and named the root cause as Einstein's own — the crew took second-day sign-off from the maid instead of the contract holder — calling it 'a coaching opportunity there for us, for sure.' Customer moved from 'I felt like I was being played' to asking for his number and volunteering referrals.
